outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Foundations of Tabular Learning and the LLM Paradigm Shift
outline.description: This chapter introduces the challenges of few-shot learning in tabular data, reviews existing approaches (traditional ML, pre-trained transformers, and direct LLM prompting), and identifies critical bottlenecks such as inference latency, prompt size limits, and the inability to access training weights for top-tier models.
subtopics: The unique characteristics and challenges of tabular data vs. NLP/CV
Overview of Few-Shot Learning regimes in machine learning
Traditional baselines: Logistic Regression, Tree Ensembles (XGBoost, Random Forest)
Pre-trained Tabular Models: TabPFN and Transfer Learning approaches
Direct LLM Integration: Serializing tables for In-Context Learning (ICL)
Limitations of current LLM-based methods: High inference cost, prompt length constraints, and dependency on fine-tuning access
Motivation for separating feature engineering from prediction

outline.description: A deep dive into the core methodology of FeatLLM. This chapter explains the conceptual shift from using LLMs as predictors to using them as automated feature engineers. It details the pipeline from raw data to rule generation, code synthesis, and final lightweight modeling.
subtopics: Core Philosophy: LLMs as Feature Engineers rather than End-to-End Predictors
High-level architecture overview: From Input Data to Final Prediction
The role of 'Rules' as interpretable intermediate features
Decoupling training (rule discovery) from inference (linear scoring)
Benefits of the architecture: Low latency inference and API-only requirements

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Prompt Engineering for Rule Extraction
outline.description: This chapter dissects the specific prompt design strategies used to force LLMs to reason logically about tabular data. It covers how to structure prompts to elicit causal reasoning before rule derivation, ensuring high-quality feature generation.
subtopics: Component 1: Basic Information Description (Task framing and Feature serialization)
Serialization formats for converting rows/columns into natural language
Step-by-step reasoning: Inferring causal tendencies before deducing rules
Mitigating spurious correlations through guided reasoning
Structuring outputs for deterministic parsing (AND/OR logic handling)
